old: To voice deep, unfulfilled wishes regarding past events ('If only... had happened!'), Hungarian introduces the sentence with *bárcsak* followed by the past tense and *volna*.
new: You know *bárcsak* from B1 Unit 5 and *bárcsak* + past conditional from B1 Unit 39. To voice an unfulfilled wish about the past ('If only... had happened!'), start the sentence with *bárcsak* and use the past tense and *volna*.
why: presents bárcsak … volna (B1 Unit 39) as new

old: When a past counterfactual condition impacts the present, the conditional clause takes the past conditional (*ha... lett volna*), while the main clause takes the present conditional (*most... lennék / tudnám*).
new: You know the past conditional (*ha* + past tense + *volna*) from B1 Unit 39 and the present conditional (*lenne*, *menne*) from A2 Unit 28. A mixed conditional uses both: when a past condition changes the present, the *ha* clause takes the past conditional (*ha... lett volna*), while the main clause takes the present conditional (*most... lennék / tudnám*).
why: no recap of the two forms the new pattern combines

old: To introduce what would have occurred had circumstances been otherwise, Hungarian uses *máskülönben* (otherwise), *ellenkező esetben* (in the contrary case), or *másként* (differently), frequently paired with *volna*.
new: You know *különben* from A2 Unit 41; *máskülönben* is its longer form. To say what would have happened if things had been different, Hungarian uses *máskülönben* (otherwise), *ellenkező esetben* (in the contrary case) or *másként* (differently), often with *volna*.
why: máskülönben is the longer form of the A2 word különben
